### Runtime Config Example Project

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/runtime-config.md

Complete example project for runtime config, including configuration, server handler, and build setup.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "nitro";

export default defineConfig({
  serverDir: "./",
  runtimeConfig: {
    apiKey: "",
  },
});
```

```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "nitro dev",
    "build": "nitro build"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "nitro": "latest"
  }
}
```

```ts
import { defineHandler } from "nitro";
import { useRuntimeConfig } from "nitro/runtime-config";

export default defineHandler((event) => {
  const runtimeConfig = useRuntimeConfig();
  return { runtimeConfig };
});
```

```json
{
  "extends": "nitro/tsconfig"
}
```

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { nitro } from "nitro/vite";

export default defineConfig({ plugins: [nitro()] });
```

### Build and start local preview for Azure Static Web Apps

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/20.providers/azure.md

Build with the azure_swa preset and start a local preview using Azure Static Web Apps CLI. Requires Azure Functions Core Tools installed.

```bash
NITRO_PRESET=azure_swa npm run build
npx @azure/static-web-apps-cli start .output/public --api-location .output/server
```

--------------------------------

### Server Fetch Example Project

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/server-fetch.md

Complete example project for server fetch. The nitro.config.ts uses the serverFetch hook to make an internal request during dev:start, while routes/index.ts uses the fetch function to call /hello internally. The package.json, tsconfig.json, and vite.config.ts provide the project setup.

```ts
import { defineConfig, serverFetch } from "nitro";

export default defineConfig({
  serverDir: "./",
  hooks: {
    "dev:start": async () => {
      const res = await serverFetch("/hello");
      const text = await res.text();
      console.log("Fetched /hello in nitro module:", res.status, text);
    },
  },
});
```

```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "nitro dev",
    "build": "nitro build"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "nitro": "latest"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "extends": "nitro/tsconfig"
}
```

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { nitro } from "nitro/vite";

export default defineConfig({ plugins: [nitro()] });
```

```ts
import { defineHandler } from "nitro";

export default defineHandler(() => "Hello!");
```

```ts
import { defineHandler } from "nitro";
import { fetch } from "nitro";

export default defineHandler(() => fetch("/hello"));
```

### Example tracing output for GET /

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/tracing.md

Shows the console timeline for a request to `/`, including the middleware, route, and storage spans with timing and attributes.

```text
▶ GET /  4.10ms  (4 spans)
  middleware GET /             █·······················   0.12ms h3.handler_type=middleware http.route=/
  GET /                        ·███████████████████·····   2.49ms h3.handler_type=route http.route=/
  getItem                      ···██····················   0.18ms db.operation=getItem db.system=memory unstorage.keys_count=1
  setItem                      ·····██··················   0.16ms db.operation=setItem db.system=memory unstorage.keys_count=1
```

### Start production server with Bun

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/10.runtimes/bun.md

Starts the production server after building with the bun preset. The output is compatible with the Bun runtime and enables Bun-specific optimizations.

```bash
bun run ./.output/server/index.mjs
```

### Add start script to package.json

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/20.providers/digitalocean.md

Add a start script to your package.json so DigitalOcean knows what command to run after a build. Then add this start script to your DigitalOcean app's run command (Components > Settings > Commands).

```json
{
   "scripts": {
      "start": "node .output/server/index.mjs"
   }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Add start and build scripts to package.json

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/20.providers/heroku.md

Defines the required 'build' and 'start' scripts in package.json for Heroku deployment.

```json5
"scripts": {
  "build": "nitro build", // or `nuxt build` if using nuxt
  "start": "node .output/server/index.mjs"
}
```

### Server entry examples for H3, Hono, Elysia, and Express

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/index.md

Server entry examples for different frameworks. Export the app from server.ts (or server.node.ts for Express) to run it for every request before routes are matched. Node-style (req, res) frameworks must use the server.node.ts filename.

```ts
import { H3 } from "h3";

const app = new H3();

app.get("/", () => "⚡️ Hello from H3!");

export default app;
```

```ts
import { Hono } from "hono";

const app = new Hono();

app.get("/", (c) => c.text("🔥 Hello from Hono!"));

export default app;
```

```ts
import { Elysia } from "elysia";

const app = new Elysia();

app.get("/", () => "🦊 Hello from Elysia!");

export default app.compile();
```

```ts
import Express from "express";

const app = Express();

app.use("/", (_req, res) => {
  res.send("Hello from Express with Nitro!");
});

export default app;
```

### Nitro + Vite + Preact SSR example files

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/vite-ssr-preact.md

Complete file set for a Nitro + Vite + Preact SSR example: package.json, tsconfig.json, vite.config.mjs, app.tsx, entry-client.tsx, entry-server.tsx, and styles.css. The entry-server.tsx uses renderToReadableStream from preact-render-to-string/stream and merges client/server assets via ?assets=client and ?assets=ssr imports.

```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "vite build",
    "preview": "vite preview",
    "dev": "vite dev"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@preact/preset-vite": "^2.10.5",
    "@tailwindcss/vite": "^4.2.2",
    "nitro": "latest",
    "preact": "^10.29.0",
    "preact-render-to-string": "^6.6.7",
    "tailwindcss": "^4.2.2",
    "vite": "latest"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "extends": "nitro/tsconfig",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "jsxImportSource": "preact"
  }
}
```

```js
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { nitro } from "nitro/vite";
import preact from "@preact/preset-vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [nitro(), preact()],
  environments: {
    client: {
      build: {
        rollupOptions: {
          input: "./src/entry-client.tsx",
        },
      },
    },
  },
});
```

```tsx
import { useState } from "preact/hooks";

export function App() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  return <button onClick={() => setCount((c) => c + 1)}>Count is {count}</button>;
}
```

```tsx
import { hydrate } from "preact";
import { App } from "./app.tsx";

function main() {
  hydrate(<App />, document.querySelector("#app")!);
}

main();
```

```tsx
import "./styles.css";
import { renderToReadableStream } from "preact-render-to-string/stream";
import { App } from "./app.jsx";

import clientAssets from "./entry-client?assets=client";
import serverAssets from "./entry-server?assets=ssr";

export default {
  async fetch(request: Request) {
    const url = new URL(request.url);
    const htmlStream = renderToReadableStream(<Root url={url} />);
    return new Response(htmlStream, {
      headers: { "Content-Type": "text/html;charset=utf-8" },
    });
  },
};

function Root(props: { url: URL }) {
  const assets = clientAssets.merge(serverAssets);
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
        {assets.css.map((attr: any) => (
          <link key={attr.href} rel="stylesheet" {...attr} />
        ))}
        {assets.js.map((attr: any) => (
          <link key={attr.href} rel="modulepreload" {...attr} />
        ))}
        <script type="module" src={assets.entry} />
      </head>
      <body>
        <h1 className="hero">Nitro + Vite + Preact</h1>
        <p>URL: {props.url.href}</p>
        <div id="app">
          <App />
        </div>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

```css
.hero {
  color: orange;
}

button {
  background-color: lightskyblue;
}
```

### render.yaml for Render.com deployment

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/20.providers/render.md

Defines a Render web service for a Nitro app. Set the name to your project name and adjust the branch as needed. The start command runs the built server, and the build command installs dependencies and builds the project. The NITRO_PRESET environment variable is set to render_com.

```yaml
services:
  - type: web
    name: <PROJECTNAME>
    env: node
    branch: main
    startCommand: node .output/server/index.mjs
    buildCommand: npx nypm install && npm run build
    envVars:
    - key: NITRO_PRESET
      value: render_com

```

--------------------------------

### amplify.yml templates for standard and monorepo setups

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/20.providers/aws-amplify.md

Two template `amplify.yml` files for advanced configuration. The first is for a standard app; the second is for a monorepo setup, using `pnpm --filter website1 build` and setting `appRoot` to `apps/website1`.

```yml
version: 1
frontend:
  phases:
    preBuild:
      commands:
        - nvm use 24 && node --version
        - corepack enable && npx --yes nypm install
    build:
      commands:
        - pnpm build
  artifacts:
    baseDirectory: .amplify-hosting
    files:
      - "**/*"
```

```yml
version: 1
applications:
  - frontend:
      phases:
        preBuild:
          commands:
          - nvm use 24 && node --version
          - corepack enable && npx --yes nypm install
        build:
          commands:
            - pnpm --filter website1 build
      artifacts:
        baseDirectory: apps/website1/.amplify-hosting
        files:
          - '**/*'
      buildPath: /
    appRoot: apps/website1
```

### Nitro Database Example Project Files

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/database.md

Complete example project files for the Nitro database feature: configuration enabling experimental database and tasks, package.json with dev/build scripts, a server handler that creates a users table and queries it, tsconfig, Vite config, and a migration task.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "nitro";

export default defineConfig({
  experimental: {
    database: true,
    tasks: true,
  },
  database: {
    default: { connector: "sqlite" },
  },
});
```

```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "nitro dev",
    "build": "nitro build"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "nitro": "latest"
  }
}
```

```ts
import { defineHandler } from "nitro";
import { useDatabase } from "nitro/database";

export default defineHandler(async () => {
  const db = useDatabase();

  // Create users table
  await db.sql`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS users`;
  await db.sql`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users ("id" TEXT PRIMARY KEY, "firstName" TEXT, "lastName" TEXT, "email" TEXT)`;

  // Add a new user
  const userId = String(Math.round(Math.random() * 10_000));
  await db.sql`INSERT INTO users VALUES (${userId}, 'John', 'Doe', '')`;

  // Query for users
  const { rows } = await db.sql`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${userId}`;

  return {
    rows,
  };
});
```

```json
{
  "extends": "nitro/tsconfig"
}
```

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { nitro } from "nitro/vite";

export default defineConfig({ plugins: [nitro()] });
```

```ts
import { defineTask } from "nitro/task";
import { useDatabase } from "nitro/database";

export default defineTask({
  meta: {
    description: "Run database migrations",
  },
  async run() {
    const db = useDatabase();

    console.log("Running database migrations...");

    // Create users table
    await db.sql`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS users`;
    await db.sql`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users ("id" TEXT PRIMARY KEY, "firstName" TEXT, "lastName" TEXT, "email" TEXT)`;

    return {
      result: "Database migrations complete!",
    };
  },
});
```

### Custom Renderer Example Files

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/renderer.md

Complete example files for a custom renderer in Nitro: configuration, renderer handler, and API route. The renderer uses Nitro's internal fetch to call the API route without network overhead.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "nitro";

export default defineConfig({
  serverDir: "./",
  renderer: { handler: "./renderer" },
});
```

```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "nitro dev",
    "build": "nitro build"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "nitro": "latest"
  }
}
```

```ts
import { fetch } from "nitro";

export default async function renderer({ url }: { req: Request; url: URL }) {
  const apiRes = await fetch("/api/hello").then((res) => res.text());
  return new Response(
    /* html */ `<!DOCTYPE html>
    <html>
    <head>
      <title>Custom Renderer</title>
    </head>
    <body>
      <h1>Hello from custom renderer!</h1>
      <p>Current path: ${url.pathname}</p>
      <p>API says: ${apiRes}</p>
    </body>
    </html>`,
    { headers: { "content-type": "text/html; charset=utf-8" } }
  );
}
```

```json
{
  "extends": "nitro/tsconfig"
}
```

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { nitro } from "nitro/vite";

export default defineConfig({ plugins: [nitro()] });
```

```ts
import { defineHandler } from "nitro";

export default defineHandler(() => "Nitro is amazing!");
```

### Virtual Routes project setup (nitro.config.ts, package.json, tsconfig.json, vite.config.ts)

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/virtual-routes.md

Complete project setup for virtual routes: config defines a virtual module and maps it to a route, package.json provides scripts and dependency, tsconfig extends Nitro's config, and vite.config.ts integrates the Nitro plugin.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "nitro";

export default defineConfig({
  routes: {
    "/": "#virtual-route",
  },
  virtual: {
    "#virtual-route": () =>
      /* js */ `export default () => new Response("Hello from virtual entry!")`,
  },
});
```

```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "nitro build",
    "dev": "nitro dev",
    "preview": "node .output/server/index.mjs"

    "nitro": "latest"
```

### Replace strings at build time

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/3.config/0.index.md

Performs build-time string replacements. The example replaces process.env.APP_VERSION with the string "1.0.0".

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  replace: {
    "process.env.APP_VERSION": JSON.stringify("1.0.0"),
  },
});
```

### package.json for vite-ssr-react-router

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/vite-ssr-react-router.md

### src/router.tsx - TanStack Router setup

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/vite-ssr-tss-react.md

Defines the router factory for the TanStack Start app. Configures preloading, error and not-found components, and scroll restoration.

```tsx
import { createRouter } from "@tanstack/react-router";
import { routeTree } from "./routeTree.gen.ts";

export function getRouter() {
  const router = createRouter({
    routeTree,
    defaultPreload: "intent",
    defaultErrorComponent: () => <div>Internal Server Error</div>,
    defaultNotFoundComponent: () => <div>Not Found</div>,
    scrollRestoration: true,
  });
  return router;
}
```

### Bring your own framework with server.ts

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/9.blog/1.v3-beta.md

Example of a server.ts entry file that exports a Hono app, demonstrating how to take full control of the HTTP layer with any framework.

```ts
import { Hono } from "hono";

const app = new Hono();
app.get("/", (c) => c.text("Hello from Hono!"));

export default app;
```

### Build and run Nitro app with Deno preset

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/10.runtimes/deno.md

Build the Nitro app with the Deno preset and start the production server using the Deno runtime. Requires the Deno CLI and the necessary permissions for network, file read, and environment access.

```bash
# Build with the Deno preset
NITRO_PRESET=deno_server npm run build

# Start production server
deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-env .output/server/index.mjs
```

### server.ts - Nitro server entry for TanStack Start

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/vite-ssr-tss-react.md

Creates the Nitro server entry point for TanStack Start. It wraps the TanStack Start handler and delegates fetch requests to it, enabling SSR in Nitro.

```ts
import handler, { createServerEntry } from "@tanstack/react-start/server-entry";

export default createServerEntry({
  fetch(request) {
    return handler.fetch(request);
  },
});
```

### server/trpc.ts - tRPC router with get and inc procedures

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/vite-trpc.md

Defines a tRPC router with a query 'get' and a mutation 'inc' that manipulate a counter. Exports the router type and a default fetch handler using fetchRequestHandler.

```ts
import { initTRPC } from "@trpc/server";
import { fetchRequestHandler } from "@trpc/server/adapters/fetch";

let counter = 0;

const t = initTRPC.create();

export const appRouter = t.router({
  get: t.procedure.query(() => {
    return { value: counter };
  }),

  inc: t.procedure.mutation(() => {
    counter++;
    return { value: counter };
  }),
});

export type AppRouter = typeof appRouter;

export default {
  async fetch(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
    return fetchRequestHandler({
      endpoint: "/trpc",
      req: request,
      router: appRouter,
    });
  },
};
```

### vite.config.mjs - Vite config for TanStack Start SSR

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/vite-ssr-tss-react.md

Vite configuration that integrates TanStack Start, React, Tailwind, and Nitro plugins. Sets the SSR build input to server.ts and enables tsconfig path resolution.

```js
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { nitro } from "nitro/vite";
import { tanstackStart } from "@tanstack/react-start/plugin/vite";
import viteReact from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
import tailwindcss from "@tailwindcss/vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [tanstackStart(), viteReact(), tailwindcss(), nitro()],
  resolve: { tsconfigPaths: true },
  environments: {
    ssr: { build: { rollupOptions: { input: "./server.ts" } } },
  },
});
```

### Cached Handler Example Files

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/cached-handler.md

Complete file tree for the cached-handler example: nitro.config.ts, package.json, server.ts, tsconfig.json, and vite.config.ts. The server.ts file uses defineCachedHandler to cache a 500ms operation and bypasses the cache when the URL contains ?skipCache=true.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "nitro";

export default defineConfig({});
```

```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "nitro dev",
    "build": "nitro build"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "nitro": "latest"
  }
}
```

```ts
import { html } from "nitro";
import { defineCachedHandler } from "nitro/cache";

export default defineCachedHandler(
  async () => {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 500));
    return html`
      Response generated at ${new Date().toISOString()} (took 500ms)
      <br />(<a href="?skipCache=true">skip cache</a>)
    `;
  },
  { shouldBypassCache: ({ req }) => req.url.includes("skipCache=true") }
);
```

```json
{
  "extends": "nitro/tsconfig"
}
```

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { nitro } from "nitro/vite";

export default defineConfig({ plugins: [nitro()] });
```

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  database: {
    default: {
      connector: "sqlite",
      options: { name: "db" },
    },
  },
});
```

### WebSocket Client Example (index.html)

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/websocket.md

This HTML file implements a WebSocket client that connects to a server at '/_ws' using the WebSocket protocol. It provides a chat interface with message sending, ping, and clear functionality. The client uses petite-vue for reactive data binding and Shiki for formatting JSON messages. It automatically connects on page load and handles reconnection by closing the previous connection.

```html
<html lang="en" data-theme="dark">
  <head>
    <title>CrossWS Test Page</title>
    <script src="https://cdn.tailwindcss.com"></script>
    <style>
      body {
        background-color: #1a1a1a;
      }
    </style>
    <script type="module">
      import { createApp, reactive, nextTick } from "https://esm.sh/petite-vue@0.4.1";

      let ws;

      const store = reactive({
        message: "",
        messages: [],
      });

      const scroll = () => {
        nextTick(() => {
          const el = document.querySelector("#messages");
          el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight;
          el.scrollTo({
            top: el.scrollHeight,
            behavior: "smooth",
          });
        });
      };

      const format = async () => {
        for (const message of store.messages) {
          if (!message._fmt && message.text.startsWith("{")) {
            message._fmt = true;
            const { codeToHtml } = await import("https://esm.sh/shiki@1.0.0");
            const str = JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(message.text), null, 2);
            message.formattedText = await codeToHtml(str, {
              lang: "json",
              theme: "dark-plus",
            });
          }
        }
      };

      const log = (user, ...args) => {
        console.log("[ws]", user, ...args);
        store.messages.push({
          text: args.join(" "),
          formattedText: "",
          user: user,
          date: new Date().toLocaleString(),
        });
        scroll();
        format();
      };

      const connect = async () => {
        const isSecure = location.protocol === "https:";
        const url = (isSecure ? "wss://" : "ws://") + location.host + "/_ws";
        if (ws) {
          log("ws", "Closing previous connection before reconnecting...");
          ws.close();
          clear();
        }

        log("ws", "Connecting to", url, "...");
        ws = new WebSocket(url);

        ws.addEventListener("message", async (event) => {
          let data = typeof event.data === "string" ? event.data : await event.data.text();
          const { user = "system", message = "" } = data.startsWith("{")
            ? JSON.parse(data)
            : { message: data };
          log(user, typeof message === "string" ? message : JSON.stringify(message));
        });

        await new Promise((resolve) => ws.addEventListener("open", resolve));
        log("ws", "Connected!");
      };

      const clear = () => {
        store.messages.splice(0, store.messages.length);
        log("system", "previous messages cleared");
      };

      const send = () => {
        console.log("sending message...");
        if (store.message) {
          ws.send(store.message);
        }
        store.message = "";
      };

      const ping = () => {
        log("ws", "Sending ping");
        ws.send("ping");
      };

      createApp({
        store,
        send,
        ping,
        clear,
        connect,
        rand: Math.random(),
      }).mount();

      await connect();
    </script>
  </head>
  <body class="h-screen flex flex-col justify-between">
    <main v-scope="{}">
      <!-- Messages -->
      <div id="messages" class="flex-grow flex flex-col justify-end px-4 py-8">
        <div class="flex items-center mb-4" v-for="message in store.messages">
          <div class="flex flex-col">
            <p class="text-gray-500 mb-1 text-xs ml-10">{{ message.user }}</p>
            <div class="flex items-center">
              <img
                :src="'https://www.gravatar.com/avatar/' + encodeURIComponent(message.user + rand) + '?s=512&d=monsterid'"
                alt="Avatar"
                class="w-8 h-8 rounded-full"
              />
              <div class="ml-2 bg-gray-800 rounded-lg p-2">
                <p
                  v-if="message.formattedText"
                  class="overflow-x-scroll"
                  v-html="message.formattedText"
                ></p>
                <p v-else class="text-white">{{ message.text }}</p>
              </div>
            </div>
            <p class="text-gray-500 mt-1 text-xs ml-10">{{ message.date }}</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
```

### Shiki server-side highlighting example files

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/shiki.md

Complete example files for server-side syntax highlighting with Shiki in Nitro. The HTML page uses a server script to call the /api/highlight endpoint, which returns highlighted HTML. The Nitro config sets serverDir to './' so the API route is picked up from the api folder. The Vite config adds the Nitro plugin. The API route uses Shiki's core highlighter with the oniguruma engine and the vitesse-dark theme.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1" />
    <title>Hello World Snippet</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css" />
  </head>
  <body>
    <div class="card" role="region" aria-label="Code snippet">
      <div class="label">JavaScript</div>
      <script server>
        const hl = (code) =>
          serverFetch("/api/highlight", {
            method: "POST",
            body: code,
          });
      </script>
      <pre><code>{{{ hl(`console.log("💚 Simple is beautiful!");`) }}}</code></pre>
    </div>
  </body>
</html>
```

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "nitro";

export default defineConfig({
  serverDir: "./",
});
```

```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "vite dev",
    "build": "vite build"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "nitro": "latest",
    "shiki": "latest"
  }
}
```

```css
html,
body {
  height: 100%;
  margin: 0;
}
body {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  background: #f6f8fa;
  font-family:
    system-ui,
    -apple-system,
    "Segoe UI",
    Roboto,
    "Helvetica Neue",
    Arial,
    "Noto Sans",
    "Liberation Sans",
    sans-serif;
}
.card {
  text-align: left;
  background: #0b1220;
  color: #e6edf3;
  padding: 1rem;
  border-radius: 8px;
  box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(2, 6, 23, 0.2);
  max-width: 90%;
  width: 520px;
}
.label {
  font-size: 12px;
  color: #9aa7b2;
  margin-bottom: 8px;
}
pre {
  margin: 0;
  font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, "Courier New", monospace;
  font-size: 14px;
  background: transparent;
  white-space: pre;
  overflow: auto;
}
```

```json
{
  "extends": "nitro/tsconfig"
}
```

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { nitro } from "nitro/vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [nitro()],
});
```

```ts
import { createHighlighterCore } from "shiki/core";
import { createOnigurumaEngine } from "shiki/engine/oniguruma";

const highlighter = await createHighlighterCore({
  engine: createOnigurumaEngine(import("shiki/wasm")),
  themes: [await import("shiki/themes/vitesse-dark.mjs")],
  langs: [await import("shiki/langs/ts.mjs")],
});

export default async ({ req }: { req: Request }) => {
  const code = await req.text();
  const html = await highlighter.codeToHtml(code, {
    lang: "ts",
    theme: "vitesse-dark",
  });
  return new Response(html, {
    headers: { "Content-Type": "text/html; charset=utf-8" },
  });
};
```
